channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Gold struggles to lure buyers as Hormuz risks and Fed hike bets counter softer USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) struggles to capitalize on the previous day's bounce from the $4,020 area, or a one-week low, and oscillates in a narrow range during the Asian session on Thursday.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Tests symmetrical triangle top above 185.50
item.description: EUR/JPY pares steadies after registering modest gains in the previous day, trading around 185.60 during the Asian hours on Thursday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar gains ground on surging Oil, rising BoC hike bets
item.description: The USD/CAD pair loses ground to near 1.4165 during the Asian trading hours on Thursday. A rise in crude oil prices provides some support to the commodity-linked Canadian Dollar (CAD) against the US Dollar (USD). Traders await the US weekly Initial Jobless Claims report later on Thursday.

item.title: Days-old Iran ceasefire dies in the Strait of Hormuz as US launches fresh strikes on Iran
item.description: The US strikes hit a rail line in Golestan province in northeastern Iran, near the border, using cruise missiles. It marked the first US strike on Iranian infrastructure since the ceasefire took hold.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD rebounds above $58.00 despite inflation fears
item.description: Silver price (XAG/USD) inches higher after three days of losses, trading around $58.30 per troy ounce during the Asian hours on Thursday.

item.title: Iran's Ghalibaf says any US military action will be met with retaliation
item.description: Iranian Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf warned the United States (US) after two days of renewed US strikes, saying that any U.S. military action will prompt retaliation. Ghalibaf emphasized that access to the Strait of Hormuz remains under Iranian control.

item.title: Euro sticks to positive bias above 1.1400 vs USD; Mideast tensions cap gains
item.description: The EUR/USD pair attracts some buyers for the second straight day, though it lacks follow-through and remains confined within the previous day's range during the Asian session on Thursday.

item.title: Australian Dollar steadies following Chinese CPI data
item.description: AUD/USD gains ground after remaining flat in the previous day, trading around 0.6930 during the Asian hours on Thursday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar holds ground despite softer China’s CPI data
item.description: NZD/USD extends its gains for the second successive day, trading around 0.5720 during the Asian hours on Thursday. The pair holds gains as the New Zealand Dollar (NZD) remains stronger following the Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation data release from New Zealand’s close trading partner, China.

item.title: China’s CPI inflation falls to 1.0% YoY in June, vs 1.1% expected
item.description: China’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) climbed 1.0% in June from a year ago after arriving at a rise of 1.2% in May, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on Thursday. The market consensus was for 1.1% in the reported period.

item.title: British Pound strengthens to near 1.3400 as UK political risk fades
item.description: The GBP/USD pair gathers strength near 1.3395 during the Asian trading hours on Thursday, bolstered by fading domestic political uncertainty.

item.title: WTI holds above $74.00, close to two-week top as bears hesitate on US-Iran/Hormuz risks
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) – the benchmark US Crude Oil price – drifts lower during the Asian session on Thursday and moves away from a two-week high, around the $75.75 region touched the previous day.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.8036 vs. 6.8077 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Thursday at 6.8036 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.8077 and 6.7978 Reuters estimate.

item.title: Japanese Yen gains ground on intervention risks
item.description: The USD/JPY pair edges lower to around 162.45 during the early Asian session on Thursday. The Japanese Yen (JPY) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) amid fears of possible intervention from Japanese authorities. The US weekly Initial Jobless Claims report is due later on Thursday.

item.title: Gold declines below $4,100 as US–Iran tensions revive inflation worries, Fed rate hike bets
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) declines to around $4,075 during the early Asian session on Thursday. The precious metal extends its downside as US President Donald Trump said the ceasefire with Iran has ended, stoking concerns that a renewal of war could again drive inflation and push up interest rates.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Downside bias as momentum improves against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Senior Technical Strategist Quek Ser Leang notes that USD/CNH has broken higher, with momentum improving after Monday’s move to 6.8051 and a close at 6.8038.

item.title: Euro steadies as Middle East strikes offsets Fed repricing
item.description: The Euro holds firm against the US Dollar on Wednesday as hostilities in the Middle East continued, with the US attacking Iran for the second straight day at around the Strait of Hormuz. At the time of writing, the EUR/USD trades at 1.1420, after bouncing off daily lows of 1.1391.

item.title: Taiwan Dollar: Flow-driven weakness with policy support – OCBC
item.description: OCBC Bank’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that Taiwan Dollar (TWD) remains on the back foot, with USD/TWD above 32, driven mainly by foreign equity selling and dividend/remittance-related US Dollar (USD) demand rather than weaker fundamentals.

item.title: The Australian Dollar flatlines while everyone else has a war to trade
item.description: AUD/USD trades pinned between 0.6900 and 0.6950 on Wednesday, essentially unchanged and printing the kind of indecision candle that tells traders the week's rebound has run out of sponsorship.

item.title: British Pound Sterling wins the day and stays stuck in the same trap
item.description: GBP/USD trades just below 1.3400 on Wednesday, up around a quarter of a percent and once again leaning on the 200-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) that has repelled every advance since the pair clawed back from its mid-June washout.

item.title: Crude Oil rediscovers its war premium as the Versailles patch peels off
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Crude Oil trades near $74.50 on Wednesday, up more than 3.5% and extending a rebound that began at the $68.00 floor in early July.

item.title: China: Growth support constrained – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Senior Asia Economist Alex Loo argues that China’s fiscal stance is turning austere as local governments prioritize debt clean-up over growth.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Market probes intervention risk – ABN AMRO
item.description: Georgette Boele at ABN AMRO highlights persistent weakness in the Japanese Yen as investors test authorities’ tolerance for depreciation. Fiscal expansion and a dovish Bank of Japan stance weigh on the currency, while Japan’s energy-importer status adds pressure.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: False breakout at 0.8100 triggers pullback
item.description: The USD/CHF pair recoils after reaching a five-day high of 0.8108 on Wednesday, edging down some 0.02% as risk appetite deteriorates due to US President Donald Trump’s suggestion of an end to the ceasefire, as Iran attacked ships on Tuesday.

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar struggles despite hawkish FOMC Minutes
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) trades near the 101.00 region on Wednesday as investors digest the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) Minutes from the June 16-17 meeting, the first under Federal Reserve (Fed) Chair Kevin Warsh.

item.title: Thai Baht: Range-bound after inflation data against dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay highlights that USD/THB edged higher as Thai inflation data support a steady policy stance. Lay links the move to expectations that the Bank of Thailand (BoT) will keep interest rates on hold at 1% through at least the next meeting.

item.title: South Korean Won: Undervaluation and BOK outlook aid won – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights an extended broad rally in South Korean Won (KRW) as Korean equities underperform, reducing rebalancing outflows.

item.title: Japanese Yen falls as Fed Minutes revive tightening bets
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) depreciates by over 0.26% against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday within familiar levels, as the Federal Reserve's (Fed) last meeting minutes showed that the majority of participants indicated that “some policy firming would likely be warranted.” The USD/JPY pair trades at 16

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Bears retain control within descending channel
item.description: EUR/USD holds firm on Wednesday after reversing earlier losses triggered by renewed tensions between the United States (US) and Iran, while traders digest the June Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting minutes.

item.title: Singapore Dollar: Short-term losses versus upside risks against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes USD/SGD is edging higher after a period of tight consolidation, with intraday upside seen as limited below nearby resistance.
